subject: science
passage: Because Earth rotates, air moving across its surface is deflected from a straight path: to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern. A large storm is a region of low pressure toward which surrounding air flows, and north of the equator the rightward deflection of that inflowing air sets the whole system turning counterclockwise, which is why hurricanes and typhoons there spin in that direction when seen from above. ______ tropical cyclones that form south of the equator, where inflowing air is deflected to the left, rotate clockwise.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The text explains that air is deflected right in the north and left in the south, and that the rightward deflection makes northern storms spin counterclockwise. The last sentence describes the reverse case: leftward deflection makes southern storms spin clockwise. A transition that introduces the opposite case is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" is tempting because the same mechanism is at work, but the outcome is the reverse (left instead of right, clockwise instead of counterclockwise), so the case is opposite, not similar.
explanation.B: Correct. "Conversely" signals that the southern case reverses the northern one: leftward deflection and clockwise rotation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The clockwise spin of southern storms is not caused by the counterclockwise spin of northern ones; each results from its own hemisphere's deflection.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Southern cyclones are not an example of northern storms spinning counterclockwise; they spin the other way.
